evidence: Identity: COLREG.2/Circ.59 (https://cimrc.shmtu.edu.cn/_upload/article/files/63/dc/35c66be74d12873254dc88a2ef00/465d5392-0ba5-4f33-8e61-a48e3499b1b3.pdf) para 1.4 quote found verbatim, annex heading 'German Bight Western Approach'. Transportstyrelsen ruttsystem.pdf lists 'German Bight western approach' (Circ.59/Circ.62), though the passage quoted in the record (Ijmuiden ... Banco del Hoyo) is not about this scheme. ISES MSC 109 summary quote found (secondary). AnlBV Anlage (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/anlbv_2004/anlage.html) Nr. 6 designates the TSS 'Tiefwasserweg' mandatory for large tankers; confirmed. The Ljubljana contents extract lists 'German Bight western approach II/14' (the quoted passage is about Cape Roca/Banco del Hoyo, not this scheme). VTS: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 quote found verbatim (report to 'German Bight Traffic' at 007 10 E 'unabhaengig davon, ob das Verkehrstrennungsgebiet German Bight Western Approach benutzt wird'); Nr. 5.1 'Der Schiffsverkehr wird im Rahmen der maritimen Verkehrssicherung ueberwacht' found. WSA page and ELWIS channel map confirm German Bight Traffic at VZ Wilhelmshaven. The statute ties the VTS entry line to ships using this TSS, which supports partial coverage of the eastern end; the western extent is correctly flagged as unverified. I could not find GBWA coordinates in the retrieved sources to confirm by plotting. Reporting: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 is the entry report owed to the VTS centre German Bight Traffic (listening watch on VTS channels after reporting). Under the rules, routine reporting owed to a VTS is not a separate mandatory reporting scheme. No IMO SOLAS V/11 system for the German Bight appears in the Transportstyrelsen mandatory SRS list (https://transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/mandatory-and-recommended-srs.pdf, 2017), but that list is not a positive statement of absence.
recommended_change: reporting: change 'Confirmed present' to 'Unresolved' (no separate mandatory SRS evidenced); move the AnlBV Nr. 3.1 report into the VTS evidence as the VTS entry report. Replace the quoted passages for S4 and S27 with the lines that actually name 'German Bight western approach'.

evidence: MSC.52(66) (https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MSCResolutions/MSC.52(66).pdf): 'The reporting system covers a circular area 35 miles in radius centred on the Ile d'Ouesant ... The TSS covers the entire area' and 'The shore-based authority is the Corsen/Ouessant vessel traffic service (voice communication sign "Ushant Traffic") installed at the CROSS CORSEN site' found verbatim. MSC.251(83) in-force 1 May 2008 quote found. COLREG.2/Circ.51 para 2(d) quote found. SDES 2024 page: 'DST Ouessant : zone de compétences CROSS Corsen' and 'soumis à un compte rendu obligatoire' found. OUESSREP is an IMO-adopted SOLAS V/11 system, so it is a separate mandatory scheme. The record says Circ.64 text was not retrieved: the Transportstyrelsen COLREG.2 compilation (https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526) contains COLREG.2/Circ.64 (4 Dec 2012), item .5 'Off Ushant (amended scheme), including article 3 of SN/Circ.232', implemented 0000 UTC 1 June 2013.
recommended_change: identity: replace 'per search result (Circ.64 text not retrieved)' with a citation to COLREG.2/Circ.64 para 1.5 and 2 in the Transportstyrelsen COLREG.2 compilation (implemented 1 June 2013).

evidence: DL 198/2006 (marinha.pt copy): preamble says MSC 79 (Dec 2004) adopted the new schemes with entry into force 1 July 2005; art. 9 quote ('Compete ao IPTM, responsavel nacional pelo servico de trafego maritimo (VTS) ...') found. DL 263/2009 art. 6 VTS area (west limit 41 51'5"N 10 14'W to 38 41'N 10 14'W to 36 30'N 9 35'W) and art. 10(4) quote on 'esquemas de separacao de trafego' found. COLREG.2/Circ.61 (shmtu copy, downloaded on second attempt after a connection reset) item .6 'Off Cape Roca' (amended), implemented 1 December 2010; annex 6 positions checked. Westmost point (26) 38 51.91N 010 13.78W is east of 010 14W. Southern points south of 38 41N (e.g. (24) 38 33.92N 010 11.69W) lie just east of the diagonal 38 41N 10 14W to 36 30N 9 35W (about 010 11.9W at that latitude), so they are inside both the VTS area and the COPREP area. MSC.278(85): area limits (north 39 45N; same west/south line) and 'shore-based authority ... is ROCA CONTROL' found. The TSS (38 33.9N to 38 51.9N) is inside. COPREP is an IMO SOLAS system, so it is separate from VTS reporting.

Transportstyrelsen COLREG.2 compilation: Circ.40 item .8 'In the Strait of Gibraltar', implemented 24 Nov 1994 (annex replaces the inshore traffic zone description, so it is an amendment); Circ.58 item .4 'In the Strait of Gibraltar (amended scheme)', implemented 1 July 2007. The record misses a later amendment in the same compilation: COLREG.2/Circ.66 (21 Nov 2014, MSC 94) annex 1 'Amendments to the existing traffic separation scheme In the Strait of Gibraltar', implemented 0000 UTC 1 June 2015. MSC.300(87) (https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MSCResolutions/MSC.300(87).pdf): 3.5.1 'Both TARIFA and TANGIER Centres monitor navigation in the TSS in the Strait of Gibraltar using radar and AIS' and 2.1 area 005 58W to 005 15W 'includes the amended traffic separation scheme' found verbatim. Tramos Feb 2025 (transportes.gob.es; 403 on the first try, loaded with a browser user agent): the quoted standfirst and the 'Tarifa Trafico ... presta el servicio de trafico maritimo en el estrecho de Gibraltar' passage were found. GIBREP is an IMO SOLAS system.
recommended_change: identity: add 'further amended by COLREG.2/Circ.66 (MSC 94), implemented 1 June 2015' to the history.

evidence: Identity: Circ.54 annex 3 'Approaches to Gulf of Venice' and Circ.58 annex 6 'Approaches to Gulf of Venice (amended)' (the separation zone is replaced by two schemes linked by a precautionary area for the LNG platform) are both in the Transportstyrelsen compilation. VTS: the Venice VTS manual (https://www.guardiacostiera.gov.it/portale/documents/d/guest/en_venezia_manuale_utentevts; 403 on the first try, loaded with a browser user agent) gives area points A 45 09.5N 012 19.9E, B 45 08.4N 012 25.7E, C 45 16.0N 012 35.0E, D 45 24.9N 012 35.0E, E 45 27.4N 012 30.7E, and the 5 NM first-call quote is found. Plotting the Circ.58 northern-part positions against line B-C: (3) 45 14.3N 012 34.0E vs line at about 012 32.9E; (4) 45 12.0N 012 31.5E vs about 012 30.1E; (6) 45 15.7N 012 35.7E vs about 012 34.6E. All TSS points lie about 1 NM seaward of the VTS limit, so the IMO scheme adjoins the VTS area but is outside it. The manual also says 'Even if not inside Venice VTS Area, vessels are bound to [respect] the North Adriatic Traffic Separation Scheme ... COLREG.2/Circ.58'. That implies the IMO TSS is outside the VTS area. Its 'TSS established in Venice VTS area' refers to the local inbound/outbound lanes on charts 222/924. The only link is the first-call obligation 5 NM before the limit, a VTS reporting duty that applies within the TSS. That is not evidence that the VTS covers the scheme. Reporting: MSC.598(111) quote found, but that revised text is implemented only from 0000 UTC 1 December 2026 (para 2). The ADRIREP now in force is MSC.139(76) annex 2, and the Venice manual names 'VENICE MRSC ("ADRIREP" Authority - IMO Res. MSC.139(76))'. The TSS is north of 40 25N, so ADRIREP applies either way.
recommended_change: vts: downgrade 'Confirmed present' to 'Unresolved' (VTS area adjoins the TSS terminus about 1 NM landward; the first call to Venice VTS is required while in the TSS, but no source places the scheme inside the VTS area). Unless the register expressly treats an adjoining VTS area with an in-TSS first-call duty as 'direct approach', in which case state that basis explicitly. reporting: cite MSC.139(76) as the text in force until 30 Nov 2026 and MSC.598(111) as the revision from 1 Dec 2026.

evidence: Circ.54 annex 3 'Approaches to/from Monfalcone' (positions 45 40.34N to 45 42.74N, 013 36.50E to 013 38.65E) is in the Transportstyrelsen compilation. VTS Trieste manual (https://www.guardiacostiera.gov.it/portale/documents/d/guest/it_trieste_manuale_utentevts): the area limits were set taking account of 'lo schema di separazione del traffico adottato con la Ris. IMO COLREG2/Circ.58 ... nella parte finale di ingresso/uscita dal porto di Monfalcone'; points A 45 43.582N 013 41.393E, B 45 42.450N 013 34.600E, C 45 36.986N 013 34.600E. The quoted 'Nell'Area VTS di Trieste e ricompreso lo schema obbligatorio ... Golfo di Trieste' is found. Strictly, that sentence refers to the Gulf of Trieste scheme, and the next sentence only says the Monfalcone scheme is set up in the same circular, so the record slightly over-reads it. However, plotting the Monfalcone TSS positions puts them wholly east of 013 34.6E and south of line B-A (about 45 42.9N at 013 37.3E), i.e. inside the VTS area. MSC.598(111) appendix lists VTS TRIESTE as an ADRIREP authority (revised text in force from 1 Dec 2026; ADRIREP currently in force under MSC.139(76)).
recommended_change: vts evidence: replace 'the manual states the Monfalcone TSS is included within the VTS area' with 'VTS area limits were drawn to include the final Monfalcone entry/exit part of the TSS; coordinate comparison places the whole Monfalcone TSS inside the area'. reporting: cite MSC.139(76) as in force until 30 Nov 2026.

evidence: Circ.40 item .5 'Strait of Canakkale', implemented 24 Nov 1994 (Transportstyrelsen compilation, OCR). KEGM page (https://kiyiemniyeti.gov.tr/vessel_traffic_and_pilotage_services): the quote is found; the service area is 'Istanbul Strait, Canakkale Strait and Marmara Sea'; VTS centre at Akbas (Canakkale). Implementing Directive (https://denizcilik.uab.gov.tr/uploads/pages/yonerge-talimat/tbdtduy.pdf; connection reset twice, loaded on the third try): Madde 12 (SP-1 via the Administration's system) and 12(3) loss of transit turn quote found; approved 04.12.2023, in force 1.1.2024. A.827(19) annex 2 para 2.1 quote found. Unofficial English 2019 Regulation Art. 7 requires SP-1 from vessels with dangerous cargo or 500 GRT and upwards 24 h ahead, and SP-2 2 h or 20 NM before entrance. TUBRAP is a named national reporting system with advance sailing plans, not only VTS routine reporting, so a national mandatory scheme is reasonable. Note that it is mandatory under Turkish law (500 GRT+/dangerous cargo); IMO only recommends participation.
recommended_change: reporting: add qualifier 'national (not IMO-adopted); SP-1 obligatory for ships of 500 GRT and upwards or carrying dangerous cargo'.

evidence: Circ.40 item .6 'Strait of Canakkale - South-West Approach' confirmed; Transportstyrelsen ruttsystem also lists 'Strait of Canakkale - South-west approach' (Circ.40). The unofficial 2019 Regulation Annex 1.5 gives the scheme at about 39 57N to 40 01.9N, 025 57.7E to 026 11.4E, seaward of the Mehmetcik-Kumkale entrance line; Art. 7(2) SP-2 is due '2 hours or 20 sea miles ... before the entrance', i.e. in this approach, but only in the unofficial translation. KEGM defines the service area as the straits and Marmara, not the approaches. Both 'Unresolved' findings are therefore proper. False-negative check (3 actions): a web search for TSVTS sector limits found only secondary material (OCIMF 2007 briefing, hosted unofficially, which says Canakkale is covered in three sectors without limits); a search for the official Turkish text of the 2019 Regulation found only mirrors (alomaliye.com, lexpera) and a Bilgi University note, and no easy official mevzuat.gov.tr copy was identified. No easy official source found.

COLREG.2/Circ.15 in the Transportstyrelsen compilation (poor OCR) lists new scheme 'Between Zaqqum and Umm Shaif oilfields' adopted at MSC 46; the ruttsystem list shows 'Between Zaqqum and Umm Shaif Colreg.2/Circ.15 1982 MSC 46'. ADNOC Port Marine Notice DZM/MN/019/2023 (https://ppa.adnoc.ae/-/media/ppa/files/marine-notices/local-marine-notices/das/2023/marine-notice-019-2023---pipe-laying-operation---traffic-arrangement-in-zaqqum-tss.ashx): 'the traffic within Zaqqum Traffic Separation Scheme will be re-arranged', and caution (d) 'Maintain a listening watch on VHF Channel 23 (Das VTIS) all times' and (g) 'inform Das VTIS' found; issued by the Harbour Master (official port authority). The notice is temporary and the Das VTIS area is not defined, but an official port authority directs ships inside the TSS to Das VTIS. That is weak but acceptable as coverage; the caveat in the record is appropriate. One extra search found other ADNOC notices citing VHF 12/23 (Das Port Control / Das VTIS) but no area definition. Reporting 'Unresolved' is proper. The Liberia MSB 14/2026 source (quote found) concerns the voluntary MSCIO area and says nothing about a mandatory scheme for this TSS, so it adds nothing.
recommended_change: vts: describe the service as a VTIS (information service) of the ADNOC Harbour Master, Port of Das, Zirku and Mubarraz, and keep the caveat that the area limits are unstated. Drop the Liberia MSB 14/2026 source as irrelevant.

evidence: Circ.44 item .10 'Off Cabo de Gata' (new scheme), implemented 1 Dec 1998, and Circ.57 item .3 (amended), implemented 1 Dec 2006; both in the Transportstyrelsen compilation. Tramos Feb 2025 (Ministerio de Transportes, text by Salvamento Maritimo; https://www.transportes.gob.es/recursos_mfom/comodin/recursos/06_los_dst_autopistas_del_mar.pdf): standfirst quote found; also 'Los DST son controlados por los servicios de trafico maritimo (STM o VTS ...) ... asignada a Salvamento Maritimo'; and 'En Espana existen sistemas de notificacion obligatoria en Fisterra y en el estrecho de Gibraltar ... mientras que en el cabo de Gata existe un sistema de notificacion voluntaria' found. La Moncloa 2015 press release quote found. The positive official statement of a voluntary-only system supports 'Confirmed absent'. It is consistent with the Transportstyrelsen 2017 mandatory SRS list, which has no Cabo de Gata entry. Caveat: the source is a ministry magazine article rather than a statute or IMO document.
